canonical_topic: Natural gas value chain and market participants
definition: The natural gas business is divided into distinct physical roles from extraction to final delivery, plus a separate financial/trading function.
core_idea: Natural gas moves through exploration, drilling/extraction, processing, transport (pipeline or tanker), storage, and local distribution, with most physical companies specializing in only one or two of these stages; trading itself is a distinct function handled by natural gas marketers.
key_points: Exploration companies locate underground natural gas reserves
Drilling companies extract gas and move it to processing facilities
Processing plants remove impurities and separate the raw gas into component hydrocarbons, yielding dry gas (methane)
Dry gas is transported to consuming regions via interstate pipeline or tanker ship, then stored until needed
Local distribution pipelines make final delivery to the end consumer
Most physical-side companies specialize narrowly because each stage is technically complex
The skills required for physical natural gas operations differ substantially from those needed to trade/speculate on the financial commodity, so trading is handled by natural gas marketers
relationships: Physical value-chain specialization is distinct from and does not overlap with financial trading expertise
trading_implications: Natural gas marketers, not upstream/midstream physical operators, are the relevant counterparties/participants for financial trading and speculation in natural gas
caveats: Assuming the same companies that extract, process, or transport natural gas are also the primary financial traders of the commodity
